entities.label: Person
entities.summary: George I, of the Bagrationi dynasty, was king of Western Georgia (Imereti) from 1389 to 1392. He was the son of Bagrat V, who ruled the kingdom from 1369 to 1389, and succeeded him upon his death. The Bagrationi dynasty was known for its strong relationships with the neighboring kingdoms of Georgia and the Golden Horde. The reign of George I was marked by a series of conflicts with the Golden Horde, which had been expanding its territories in the region. The kingdom of Imereti was eventually absorbed into the Grand Duchy of Georgia in 1440. George I's legacy is significant in the history of the region, as he played a key role in shaping the political landscape of Western Georgia during the 14th century. The Bagrationi dynasty continued to rule the region for centuries, leaving a lasting impact on the culture and politics of the area.
